findings.reason: Original standalone tiles contain the complete argument but no picture. A concrete boundary-torus diagram materially clarifies the decisive distinction between the contractible attaching circle and the essential belt meridian, and makes the bounding-disk disjointness visible. A quotient-square view shows this more precisely than a perspective solid torus.
findings.action: Added a final Remarks section with a fenced TikZ fundamental-domain schematic and prose connecting its empty intersection and contractible circle to existing steps 1.1–3.1.

correction: Added an explanatory boundary-torus diagram of the belt meridian B and the disk D with attaching circle gamma=boundary D, disjoint from B. Preserved original statement, facts, proof and all frontmatter byte-for-byte.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The quotient rectangle models partial W1=S1 x S1; horizontal coordinate is the first factor and vertical coordinate the second.
diagram_math_checks.check: Opposite edges are identified as stated in the caption. The vertical segment at x=0.8 has identified endpoints and is therefore the closed meridian B={p} x S1.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original Counterexample step 1.1 and Fact F1 identify this exact product torus and belt meridian; the k-handle definition gives the n=3,k=1 belt sphere as S1.

diagram_math_checks.objects: D is the Euclidean closed disk centered at (2.7,1.3) with radius 0.55; gamma is its boundary.
diagram_math_checks.check: D lies entirely in the rectangle interior: x lies in [2.15,3.25] within (0,4), and y lies in [0.75,1.85] within (0,2.6). Thus its quotient image is an embedded disk, with gamma a contractible circle on the boundary torus.
diagram_math_checks.justification: This depicts the precise choice in original Statement refuted and step 1.1, without making gamma the essential meridian.

diagram_math_checks.objects: B and D in the boundary torus.
diagram_math_checks.check: The disk has x>=2.15 whereas B has x=0.8, and neither disk nor circle reaches the identified edges. Therefore D intersect B is empty and gamma intersect B is empty. No crossings or orientations are asserted. The integer and mod-two intersection numbers are both zero.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original step 2.1 and Fact F2; the local attaching-belt intersection-matrix definition counts intersections of the attaching and belt circles.

diagram_math_checks.objects: Attaching h2 along gamma and fundamental groups.
diagram_math_checks.check: The caption repeats the existing calculation: gamma bounds D in partial W1, so its relation in pi1(W1) is trivial; pi1(W1 union h2)=Z, whereas pi1(W0)=1. The diagram is of the boundary before attachment, not a claimed image of the resulting manifold.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original step 2.2 uses the pushout calculation and step 3.1 obstructs cancellation. The rigorous proof remains independent of the figure.
